findings.title: Admin handoff state survives later user handoff and disables managed writer fencing despite R04/R05 being marked complete
findings.description: The Online adapter stores `request.session.stcontrolAdmin` during admin handoff, never clears it during later user handoff, and `stcontrolRequestTracker` exits early whenever that admin marker exists. A browser session that performs admin handoff first and user handoff second can continue user writes without the managed lease, stale-writer, or idle-session fencing that `docs/requirements-traceability.md` declares closed for R04 and R05.
findings.recommendation: Clear `stcontrolAdmin` before completing a user handoff, clear any stale managed user envelope before completing an admin handoff, and add a regression that reuses one cookie across admin -> user handoff and proves `stale_writer_session` / lease fencing still applies.
findings.impact: Current code leaves a confirmed write-path bypass in the shipped Online adapter while the acceptance matrix records R04 and R05 as completed, so the closure claim is false and cross-node single-writer guarantees are not actually enforced for mixed admin/user sessions.

metadata.missing_test: no mixed admin->user cookie reuse regression exists in the Online suites

findings.title: Managed browser cookies are auto-promoted to independent mode without forced re-login on the request path
findings.description: When the adapter enters independent mode, `stcontrolRequestTracker` calls `canUseNativeLogin(handle)` for any non-independent session envelope and rewrites the in-memory envelope to `independent` on an arbitrary request. That bypasses the explicit `/api/users/login` password flow and takeover-confirmation path that `users-public.js` and the disaster-login tests use as the intended disaster-mode gate.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed when an old managed envelope appears during `independent` or `independent-draining`, and only create `INDEPENDENT` session envelopes from a successful `/api/users/login` request that has just passed password and takeover checks. Add a tracker-level regression that starts with a managed cookie, flips the adapter to independent mode, and verifies the next write is rejected until the user logs in again.
findings.impact: Existing managed browser sessions can survive a controller outage and become disaster-write sessions without a fresh password login, which leaves R02 and the disaster-mode acceptance path materially weaker than the requirement matrix claims.

findings.title: Acceptance closure is still blocked because the 80% gate is unmet and the real process/cross-repo suites are optional skips
findings.description: The current acceptance artifact still states that combined cross-platform coverage is 66.7% and cannot justify '上线完成'. At the same time, the real PostgreSQL process acceptance test and the Go<->Online cross-repository adapter test both skip in short mode and whenever DSN / Node / fixtures are unavailable, so a default green `go test ./...` does not satisfy the review state's target `all_confirmed_requirements_closed_and_basic_tests_green`.
findings.snippet: 总覆盖率仍远低于最终 80% 门禁，不能据此宣称上线完成。
findings.recommendation: Promote the DSN-backed PostgreSQL + process + cross-repo suites into required acceptance commands/CI jobs instead of opt-in skips, publish one reproducible acceptance entrypoint that runs them, and keep P3 / release closure open until the documented 80% gate is actually reached or formally revised.
findings.impact: The repository still lacks an enforced acceptance harness for the very tests that exercise real PostgreSQL, process restarts, and cross-repository adapter behavior, so the requested P0->P3 acceptance closure is not currently auditable or releasable.

cross_references.reason: Mixed admin/user session state contaminates the request-path trust boundary and invalidates the documented single-writer/session-fencing design.
Independent-mode request conversion weakens the intended re-authentication boundary and leaves outage behavior inconsistent with the public login flow.
Acceptance evidence is not enforced by the default test path, so deployment readiness and regression confidence remain overstated.
